narrative.overview:
The public catalog is a printed form lying on an indigo desk. White form paper is ruled in a single indigo form ink; questions are boxed fields with small printed captions; the three verticals are carbon copies of the same form in pink (beauty), canary (aesthetics) and sky blue (dental); the one action ink is a violet rubber stamp. Businesses appear as numbered tear-off tickets with die-cut notches and a dashed perforation between stub and body. Every device is something a real appointment card, carbon triplicate or ticket roll actually has.

Density is that of a form: hairline rules (1.5px ink, 1px pale rule) carry structure, not cards floating on whitespace. Desk bands (header, hero, business band, footer) frame the paper; paper set on the desk keeps paper colours. Headlines are condensed, very heavy Georgian set at narrow width; every number (dates, ticket №, counts, domain) is typewriter mono with tabular digits. Motion is physical and short: sheets slide, tabs lift, tickets rise a few pixels, all on one out-expo curve, and all of it switches off under reduced motion.

The business panel (Operate mode, /app/*) is the back office of the same card. Navigation sits on the indigo desk as a rail; work happens on form paper in sheet-white sheets ruled with a 1.5px ink head rule. The calendar is a timetable board on which every booking is a small torn-off ticket whose stub is coloured by status. Operate mode is denser than the catalog: a smaller type ramp, 2.25rem controls on desktop, one compact head row per page, and no explanatory paragraphs.

The world explicitly rejects the category default it replaces: a soft pink gradient banner carousel over rows of rounded photo cards, and in the panel a pastel SaaS dashboard with gradient hero headers, coloured metric cards and pill buttons. No glass and no decorative colour gradients.
keyCharacteristics: One indigo ink for all text and rules; one violet stamp for actions, statuses and promotion marks.

Vertical colour is carbon-copy colour: it owns a whole region (tab, sheet, stub, ledger head), never a stray accent. In the panel, canary and sky also carry booking status on ticket stubs and status marks, under the named Status Stub exception.
Square-ish corners (2-6px), hairline rules, perforations and die-cut notches as the edge language.
Condensed heavy Georgian display; mono tabular numerals for anything counted, timed or dated.
Soft, ink-tinted drop shadows only where paper sits on the desk or lifts on interaction.
Panel: desk rail, one head row, sheets, ticket board.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Text and structural rules are Form Ink (or Faded Ink for secondary). No second text colour exists on paper; on a carbon tint, use that vertical's own ink.

rules.name: The Carbon Copy Rule
rules.body: A vertical colour fills a whole region tied to that vertical (tab, sheet, ticket stub, ledger head, tint of the chosen card at 16%, the org's vertical chip on the rail). It is never used as a generic accent, button colour, or decoration detached from a vertical. The one sanctioned exception is the Status Stub Rule below.

rules.name: The Status Stub Rule
rules.body: In Operate mode, booking status is printed on the ticket stub and on status marks with a fixed vocabulary: pending = Carbon Canary stub with Form Ink glyph; confirmed = Carbon Sky with Dental Ink; checked-in and in-service = Rubber-Stamp Violet with white; completed = Pale Rule with Form Ink; cancelled and no-show = a 45deg hatch of Pale Rule (3px on, 3px off), dashed ticket border and the client name struck through in Faded Ink. Status marks follow the same map (warning = canary with a violet outline, info = sky, success = pale rule, danger = ruled wash struck through, violet = stamp fill). Every stub also carries a line icon and, where height allows, the status word, so status never rides on colour alone. Carbon Pink is never a status colour. Outside the stub and the mark, canary and sky mean their vertical only.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Violet means "act" or "officially marked". Primary actions, links to book, focus, promotion/status stamps, the now-line, and the in-service stub; nothing else.

rules.name: The Stamped Numeral Rule
rules.body: Every date, time, count, price, ticket number and the domain is set in Martian Mono with tabular digits. Prose never is.

rules.name: The Condensed Voice Rule
rules.body: Emphasis comes from width and weight (75-90% width, 800-850), not from a second display family or colour.

rules.name: The Text Floor Rule
rules.body: Georgian text never goes below 0.72rem; mono numerals may go to 0.7rem. Density comes from fewer words, not smaller ones.

rules.name: The Paper Only Lifts Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest except the card on the desk and the pinned board ticket's 1px contact shadow. Every other shadow is a response to state: chosen, pressed, hovered. Panel sheets, metrics and toolbars carry no shadow.

dos: Do set all text and structural rules in Form Ink on paper, and each vertical's own ink on its tint.
Do give every vertical its full carbon-copy pair and use it for whole regions (tab, sheet, stub, ledger head).
